verses.text: In the eighteenth year that Jeroboam son of Nebat was king, Abijam became king of Judah.
He ruled in Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.
He did all the same sins his father had done before him. His heart was not fully true to the LORD his God, as the heart of his ancestor David had been.
But for David's sake, the LORD his God gave Abijam a lamp in Jerusalem. He gave him a son to rule after him, and he kept Jerusalem strong.
He did this because David had done what was right in the LORD's eyes. All his life David never turned away from anything the LORD commanded him, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam as long as Abijam lived.
The rest of what Abijam did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah. There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
Abijam died and was buried in the city of David. His son Asa became king after him.
In the twentieth year that Jeroboam was king of Israel, Asa became king of Judah.
He ruled in Jerusalem for forty-one years. His grandmother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.
Asa did what was right in the LORD's eyes, as his ancestor David had done.
He drove the male shrine prostitutes out of the land and got rid of all the idols his ancestors had made.
He even removed his grandmother Maacah from being queen mother, because she had made a disgusting image for the goddess Asherah. Asa cut down her image and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
The high places were not removed, but Asa's heart was fully true to the LORD all his life.
He brought into the LORD's temple the silver, the gold, and the objects that he and his father had set apart for God.
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel as long as they both lived.
Baasha king of Israel attacked Judah. He built up the town of Ramah so that no one could go in or out to Asa king of Judah.

Then Asa took all the silver and gold that was left in the treasuries of the LORD's temple and of the king's palace. He gave it to his officials and sent them to Ben-Hadad king of Syria, who lived in Damascus. Ben-Hadad was the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion. Asa said,

"Let us make a treaty, as there was between my father and your father. Look, I am sending you a gift of silver and gold. Go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so he will leave me alone."
Ben-Hadad agreed with King Asa. He sent his army commanders to attack the towns of Israel. They conquered Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, all of Chinneroth, and all the land of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard about it, he stopped building Ramah and stayed in Tirzah.
Then King Asa gave an order to all Judah, and no one was excused. They carried away the stones and wood Baasha had been using to build Ramah. With them King Asa built up Geba in Benjamin, and Mizpah.
The rest of what Asa did, all his power, all his deeds, and the towns he built, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah. But when he was old, he got a disease in his feet.
Asa died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of his ancestor David. His son Jehoshaphat became king after him.
Jeroboam's son Nadab became king of Israel in the second year that Asa was king of Judah. Nadab ruled Israel for two years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He followed the ways of his father and the sin his father had made Israel commit.
Baasha son of Ahijah, from the tribe of Issachar, made a plot against Nadab. Baasha killed him at Gibbethon, a Philistine town that Nadab and all Israel were attacking.
Baasha killed Nadab in the third year that Asa was king of Judah, and became king in his place.
As soon as Baasha became king, he killed Jeroboam's whole family. He did not leave Jeroboam anyone alive. He destroyed them all, just as the LORD had said through his servant Ahijah from Shiloh.
This happened because of the sins Jeroboam had committed and had made Israel commit, and because he had made the LORD, the God of Israel, angry.
The rest of what Nadab did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel as long as they both lived.
In the third year that Asa was king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king of all Israel in Tirzah. He ruled for twenty-four years.
He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. He followed the ways of Jeroboam and the sin Jeroboam had made Israel commit.
